name: Antiquities on the Loose

abilities.text: Create two 2/2 red and white Spirit creature tokens. Then if ~ was cast from anywhere other than your hand, put a +1/+1 counter on each Spirit you control.

notes: 'cast from anywhere other than your hand' is the ELSE branch of the cast-from-hand condition - an exact negation, not an approximation: the then branch is deliberately empty. The counters go on each Spirit you control (the two new tokens included) through for-each.

issues: Create two 2/2 red and white Spirit creature tokens. — expected Two tokens named 'Spirit' (a token's name is its subtypes), 2/2, red and white, Creature — Spirit. — scripted token {count:2, 2/2, colors:['R','W'], types:['Creature'], subtypes:['Spirit']} with no `name`; game.ts:1379 then derives 'Spirit token'. Cosmetic, and consistent with the repo convention (a `name` is written only for named tokens — Treasure, Germ, Lander, Eldrazi Spawn). It is NOT the cause of the 0/3 blind result: tokens are built from the source card's def, so scenarioDsl's findByName sees 'Antiquities on the Loose' regardless of any script-side name — a harness limitation. — CR CR 111.4

Then if this spell was cast from anywhere other than your hand, put a +1/+1 counter on each Spirit you control. — expected Exact negation of 'cast from your hand' (true for the flashback cast from the graveyard, false for a hand cast, false for an uncast copy); counters go on every Spirit permanent you control, the two new tokens included. — scripted conditional {kind:'cast-from-hand'} with an empty `then` and the work in `else`; characteristics.ts:432 reads (src.castWith?.from ?? 'hand') === 'hand', so a copy that was never cast takes the empty branch — matching the card. for-each over {subtypes:['Spirit'], who:'you'} defaults to the battlefield and runs after the token op, so the new tokens are covered. Correct; the blind run confirms both branches and that the opponent's Spirit is untouched. — CR CR 608.2, 702.34a

Flashback {4}{W}{W} — expected Castable from the graveyard for {4}{W}{W}, then exiled. — scripted altCosts {id:'flashback', cost {4}{W}{W}, from:'graveyard', exileAfter:true} with a covers entry claiming the line. Correct; the blind exile/graveyard-count assertions pass. — CR CR 702.34a

Create two 2/2 red and white Spirit creature tokens. — expected Two tokens named 'Spirit', 2/2, red and white, creature - Spirit. — scripted token count 2, 2/2, colors ['R','W'], types ['Creature'], subtypes ['Spirit'], no `name`, so game.ts:1379 names them 'Spirit token' instead of 'Spirit'. Purely cosmetic; it does NOT cause the blind failures either, since token def.name is inherited from the source card (the harness's findByName reads def.name), so setting `name` would not fix them. — CR CR 111.4

Then if this spell was cast from anywhere other than your hand, put a +1/+1 counter on each Spirit you control. — expected Exact negation of 'cast from your hand' - true for the flashback cast from the graveyard, false for a hand cast; a counter on every Spirit permanent you control, the two new tokens included. — scripted conditional {kind:'cast-from-hand'} with an empty `then` and the work in `else`; characteristics.ts:449 reads (src.castWith?.from ?? 'hand') === 'hand' against the zone recorded at cast (game.ts:641). The else branch runs for-each over {subtypes:['Spirit'], who:'you'}, which defaults to the battlefield (refs.ts:139) and runs after the token op, so the fresh tokens get counters and the opponent's Spirits do not. Correct. — CR CR 608.2 / 400.7

Flashback {4}{W}{W} — expected Castable from the graveyard for {4}{W}{W}; exiled instead of going back to the graveyard. — scripted altCosts entry id 'flashback', {4}{W}{W}, from:'graveyard', exileAfter:true, plus a covers entry claiming the line. Correct - the blind run confirms the card ends in exile, not the graveyard. — CR CR 702.34a
